title: Network properties: accumulation, ordering, and coding
text: accumulate_downstream() propagates per-feature attribute (drainage area, incremental length, anything additive) downstream, summing upstream contributions confluences. runs single topological sort followed one O(E) edge pass, scales continental networks. Consider two headwaters (1, 2) joining 3, flows outlet 4: Feature 3 accumulates 1.0 + 2.0 + 0.5 = 3.5, outlet inherits full basin total. column names default flowpath_id / flowpath_toid can overridden via id toid arguments match network table (including reference-fabric id/toid). cyclic network rejected rather silently producing wrong totals:
code: df <- data.frame(   flowpath_id   = c("1", "2", "3", "4"),   flowpath_toid = c("3", "3", "4", "0"),   area          = c(1.0, 2.0, 0.5, 0.0) )  accumulate_downstream(df, attr = "area") #> [1] 1.0 2.0 3.5 3.5 cyclic <- data.frame(   flowpath_id   = c("1", "2"),   flowpath_toid = c("2", "1"),   area          = c(1, 1) )  accumulate_downstream(cyclic, attr = "area") #> Error in `accumulate_downstream()`: #> ! Network contains cycles; cannot accumulate.

title: Network properties: accumulation, ordering, and coding
text: get_hydroseq() assigns total topological ordering network. Larger values upstream; value decreases monotonically move toward outlet, makes convenient sort key downstream traversal.
code: df$hydroseq <- get_hydroseq(df) df[order(-df$hydroseq), c("flowpath_id", "flowpath_toid", "hydroseq")] #>   flowpath_id flowpath_toid hydroseq #> 4           4             0        4 #> 2           2             3        3 #> 1           1             3        2 #> 3           3             4        1

title: Network properties: accumulation, ordering, and coding
text: rest family builds standard NHDPlus-style routing attributes top topological pass. Take small basin, mainstem 4 -> 3 -> 1 tributary 2 -> 1 draining outlet 1: get_streamorder(), Strahler order: leaves 1, order increases two equal-order streams meet (confluence 1 order 2). get_levelpath(), groups reaches continuous mainstems, following largest-weight contributor confluence (arbolate sum, 1, 3, 4 share level path tributary 2 ). get_pathlength(), distance along network reach’s outlet network terminus (0 outlet, summing downstream lengths going ). get_streamlevel(), many level-path steps reach terminus: mainstem 1, tributary 2.
code: net <- data.frame(   flowpath_id   = c("1", "2", "3", "4"),   flowpath_toid = c("0", "1", "1", "3"),   lengthkm      = c(4, 2, 3, 5) )  net$arbolate  <- accumulate_downstream(net, attr = "lengthkm")   # arbolate sum net$order     <- get_streamorder(net)                            # Strahler order net$levelpath <- get_levelpath(net, weight = "arbolate")         # mainstem grouping net$pathlen   <- get_pathlength(net, length = "lengthkm")        # distance to outlet net$level     <- get_streamlevel(net, levelpath = "levelpath")   # stream level net #>   flowpath_id flowpath_toid lengthkm arbolate order levelpath pathlen level #> 1           1             0        4       14     2         4       0     1 #> 2           2             1        2        2     1         1       4     2 #> 3           3             1        3        8     1         4       4     1 #> 4           4             3        5        5     1         4       7     1

title: Network properties: accumulation, ordering, and coding
text: get_pfafstetter() assigns hierarchical Pfafstetter basin codes. needs total drainage area, hydrosequence, level paths precomputed, subdivides basin’s mainstem four largest tributaries, recursing max_level digits deep: result meaningful full basin, digit narrows location within drainage hierarchy. four-reach toy network tributaries large enough subdivide, every code comes back NA.
code: # on a real fabric this is accumulated catchment area; `arbolate` stands in here net$total_da_sqkm <- net$arbolate net$topo_sort     <- get_hydroseq(net) net$pfaf          <- get_pfafstetter(net, max_level = 2)

title: Network properties: accumulation, ordering, and coding
text: upstream_index() assigns feature nested set pair, upstream_id (depth-first pre-order position) num_upstreams (many features sit strictly ). Together turn “everything upstream X” integer range test rather graph traversal: Everything upstream feature upstream_id == u num_upstreams == k exactly half-open range (u, u + k]: walk expands largest-upstream branch first, mainstem stays contiguous. Note upstream_id build-specific: changes whenever topology changes, index, persistent key. hydrofabric whose flowpaths route nexuses, hf_upstream_index() resolves flowpath -> nexus -> flowpath hops first indexes resulting flowpath graph. write_hydrofabric() calls , written GeoPackage carries index already. merge_groups() builds pre-order cut network contiguous runs, breaking wherever feature flow directly predecessor (order) wherever given order column changes. group contiguous upstream_id range, size-budgeted partitioner can merge whole groups always end complete sub-networks: mainstem 4 -> 3 -> 1 forms one group; tributary 2 .
code: idx <- upstream_index(net) cbind(net["flowpath_id"], idx) #>   flowpath_id upstream_id num_upstreams #> 1           1           1             3 #> 2           2           4             0 #> 3           3           2             1 #> 4           4           3             0 u <- idx$upstream_id[net$flowpath_id == "1"] k <- idx$num_upstreams[net$flowpath_id == "1"] net$flowpath_id[idx$upstream_id > u & idx$upstream_id <= u + k] #> [1] "2" "3" "4" merge_groups(net, order = "levelpath") #> [1] 1 2 1 1
